messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Distance for Windows and R 4.2
parts:
This message is relevant for users of Distance for Windows who make use
of the analysis engines that call R - that is the MRDS, DSM and MA
analysis engines.

In the most recent release of R, that is version 4.2, the R for Windows
build has stopped supporting 32-bit R. This is the version called by
Distance for Windows. Hence, at present Distance for Windows is not
compatible with the latest version of R. We therefore suggest users do
not upgrade beyond R 4.1.2, which is the version supported by our
current release of Distance for Windows (version 7.4 Release 2). If
users do wish to upgrade their version of R, they should retain version
4.1.2 on their computer so that Distance for Windows can still call it
to run the analysis engines.

We are planning a new release of Distance for Windows for the end of
July (version 7.5 Release 1) that will fix this issue.

Best wishes, Len Thomas

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Distance for Windows and R 4.2
parts:
Thanks for writing Leo, and apologies for not updating the list.

We have postponed the planned release to August 23rd. This is because we are
planning a release of the R package mrds and would like to be able to include it
in the Distance for Windows release. (The mrds package is used in the MRDS
analysis engine, for analyses of mark-recapture distance sampling data.) I'm
sorry for the delay.

In general, Distance for Windows planned release dates should be available as
"milestones" on the site where users can report issues,

https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/distance-bugs/

A direct link to the milestones list (there's only 1 at present, which is
Distance 7.5) is

https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/distance-bugs/milestones

With best wishes,

Len
